stem:
Adil works with the Virahanka sequence that begins $1$, $2$, $3$, $5$, $8$, $13$. Each next term is the sum of the two previous terms.

Which two claims correctly extend the sequence and its parity pattern?

options.text: Any single listed term already fixes every later term with no sum rule.
The next term after $8$ and $13$ is $8+13=21$, which is odd.
From $1$ (odd), $2$ (even), $3$ (odd), the parity pattern odd, even, odd continues, so the term $21$ is odd.
The same forward sum rule also covers every unrelated arithmetic sequence in the chapter.

teacher.key_rationale: Next Virahanka term is the sum of the previous two, and parity cycles odd, even, odd. Skipping the sum rule, or stretching it to every arithmetic sequence, leaves the hinge.
